text:
The goal column says one. Everything else says Charlie McAvoy is playing some of the best hockey of his career. Boston has taken 62% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five-on-five with him on the ice, nearly 12 points better than without him, and he does it in 24:16 a night. Evolving-Hockey had him 30th of 215 defensemen by wins above replacement last season, mostly from even-strength offense, against competition in the 95th percentile.

The points are arriving as assists: seven in his last ten games, no goals. His shooting percentage sits at 4.8%, below even the low end of our range for him, which is the kind of number that tends to climb. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking calls him a setup man (5.6 primary shot assists per 60, 83rd percentile among defensemen), so watch where the puck goes after he touches it.

One caution runs the other way. The Bruins have scored about four more goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, and that kind of luck usually fades. Our projection has him around 59 points by season's end, with a range of 47 to 71.
